sections.h2: Where do I find and record property records in King County, Texas?
sections.html:
Deeds and other land papers for King County are recorded by the County Clerk in Guthrie, and the clerk's web page links to an online records search. Walk-in visitors go to 800 South Baker; mail goes to P.O. Box 135, Guthrie, TX 79236. The telephone number is 806.596.4412 and the fax is 806.596.4664.

The clerk's page asks people who send a document by mail to include a self-addressed envelope for its return. No fee total is printed beside that request, and hours are not posted, so phone the office before you put a check in the mail.

  • The original deed with ink signatures and the notary's acknowledgment
  • A mailing address for every grantee, since leaving it off can trigger an extra charge
  • An envelope addressed to yourself with postage on it
  • A check for whatever amount the clerk quotes

sections.h2: Which King County offices handle which part of a property file?
sections.html:
Three offices in Guthrie split the work on any parcel. The clerk keeps recorded documents, the chief appraiser keeps value and exemption files, and the tax assessor-collector sends statements and takes payments. Each lists its own post office box on the county website.

The appraisal office also posts board meeting notices on its county page, which helps if you want to know when the board that oversees valuations next meets.

sections.h2: What must a deed show before the King County Clerk will record it?
sections.html:
Texas will not let a clerk record a land conveyance unless the signature was acknowledged, or sworn before two witnesses (Property Code 12.001(b)). The 2023 county clerk manual lists what goes into the deed records: warranty deeds of both kinds, quitclaims, trustee's, sheriff's and tax deeds, releases of liens, leases, powers of attorney and several affidavits.

That manual also explains how the bill is built. Page one carries $5.00 and each added page $4.00 under Local Government Code 118.012, and records management, archive and technology charges come on top within statutory caps. Because each county picks its own add-ons, the King County total will differ from the base numbers, so ask the office for the whole amount.

Land records follow the land. A deed for a King County house goes to Guthrie, wherever the seller now lives, whether that is Lubbock, Wichita Falls or another state.

sections.h2: What kind of county is King County, Texas?
sections.html:
King County is among the smallest counties in the nation by population. The Census Bureau shows about 192 people for mid-2025, against 265 in the 2020 census and 286 in 2010. Its 910.87 square miles of land hold roughly 0.3 people per square mile.

The Handbook of Texas places the county in the Rolling Prairie region of northwest Texas, with Cottle, Foard, Knox, Stonewall and Dickens counties around it. The legislature created it on August 21, 1876, and it was organized in 1891 with Guthrie as county seat. Big ranches drove its early story: the Four Sixes, the Pitchfork, the Matador and the SMS. Oil came in 1943, and beef cattle remain the main farm product. U.S. 83 runs north and south, U.S. 82 east and west, and Dumont and Finney are the other named communities. The handbook calls Guthrie, with about 160 people when the entry was written, the largest town and the seat of government, which is why county records business all lands in that one town.

The 2020 to 2024 survey counts 111 households averaging 1.90 people and 177 housing units. Owners occupy 59.5 percent of homes, a typical owned home is valued at $52,100, and nearly one in four people, 22.9 percent, is 65 or older.

sections.h2: What record problems come up when selling a house in King County?
sections.html:
Three snags recur: an owner who died before title was cleared, a lien nobody released, and a tax bill left unpaid. The clerk's recorded documents and the tax office files show each one, and Texas has a defined fix for each.

  • Owner died, no probate. A will may be probated within four years of death. A small estate affidavit fits only when there was no will, the assets (not counting homestead and exempt property) total $75,000 or less, and all heirs agree. A court must approve it.
  • Heirship by affidavit. A sworn heirship statement filed with the clerk is possible, yet no law forces a lender or title insurer to accept it.
  • Old mortgage. A paid-off lender should sign a release, which the clerk records like any other instrument. Request one if the payoff happened years ago.
  • Ranch or oil acreage. When a house sits on part of a larger tract, have the title agent trace whether earlier deeds reserved minerals.

Closing agents run the lien, judgment and heir searches before funds move, so these items surface early.

sections.h2: How do King County property taxes fit into a sale?
sections.html:
King County bills come from local taxing units, since the state levies no property tax of its own. The appraisal district values each parcel as of January 1, and spring notices from the chief appraiser start the protest clock: file by May 15, or by the 30th day after the notice reaches you if that date falls later. Appeals past the review board can go to district court or binding arbitration.

Statements go out about October 1 with payment due by January 31. On February 1 an unpaid bill turns delinquent and picks up six percent in penalty plus one percent interest. The lien for each year's tax attaches on January 1, which means the title cannot be fully clear while a prior year remains open. The King County Tax Assessor-Collector can quote what a particular parcel owes.

For rates and exemptions, see our King County property tax guide.

sections.h2: How can a cash sale work when the King County records are messy?
sections.html:
An as-is cash purchase can still close when the deed history needs cleanup, because the title agent handles the paperwork instead of the seller doing repairs and showings. Tell us what you found in the records, such as a missing heir or an old lien, and we will explain how a sale could move forward.

The closing documents are recorded with the King County Clerk afterward. The title agent confirms payoff figures on any recorded mortgage and collects taxes due at the table.

faqs.q: Who records deeds in King County, Texas?
faqs.a: The King County Clerk in Guthrie does. Texas makes the county clerk the county recorder, so every deed for a King County house is filed at that single office.

faqs.q: Can I send a deed to the King County Clerk by mail?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as you add a self-addressed envelope, which the clerk's page asks for. Phone 806.596.4412 to get the fee, then mail the original signed and acknowledged deed showing a grantee mailing address.

faqs.q: Where do I dispute my King County appraisal?
faqs.a: Begin with the chief appraiser at P.O. Box 117 in Guthrie. A written protest to the appraisal review board is due May 15 or by the 30th day after the notice is delivered, whichever comes later.

faqs.q: What if the owner of a King County house died without probate?
faqs.a: Several routes exist: probating a will inside four years, a small estate affidavit for modest estates, a muniment of title, or an affidavit of heirship. The right one depends on whether a will exists and who the heirs are.

faqs.q: How many people live in King County, Texas?
faqs.a: About 192 as of mid-2025 by Census Bureau estimate, down from 265 in the 2020 census. The same source lists 177 housing units and a $52,100 typical value for owned homes in the 2020 to 2024 survey.
